content: Caution is advised when prescribing TOBI® to patients with known or suspected renal, auditory, vestibular, or neuromuscular dysfunction. Patients receiving concurrent parenteral aminoglycoside therapy should be monitored as clinically appropriate. Aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant women. These drugs cross the placenta, and streptomycin has been associated with several reports of total, irreversible, bilateral congenital deafness in pediatric patients exposed in utero. Patients who use TOBI® during pregnancy or become pregnant while taking TOBI® should be informed of the potential risk to the fetus. Ototoxicity, as measured by complaints of hearing loss or audiometric evaluations, was not observed with TOBI® therapy during clinical studies. However, transient tinnitus occurred in eight TOBI®-treated patients compared to none in the placebo group during these studies. Tinnitus may serve as an early warning sign of ototoxicity, and its onset warrants caution. Ototoxicity, manifesting as both auditory and vestibular toxicity, has been reported with parenteral aminoglycosides. Vestibular toxicity may present as vertigo, ataxia, or dizziness. In post-marketing experience, patients receiving TOBI® have reported hearing loss, some of which occurred in individuals with prior or concurrent treatment with systemic aminoglycosides. Patients with hearing loss frequently reported tinnitus. Nephrotoxicity was not observed during TOBI® clinical studies but has been associated with aminoglycosides as a drug class. If nephrotoxicity occurs in a patient receiving TOBI®, tobramycin therapy should be discontinued until serum concentrations fall below 2 μg/mL. TOBI® should be used cautiously in patients with neuromuscular disorders, such as myasthenia gravis or Parkinson’s disease, as aminoglycosides may exacerbate muscle weakness due to a potential curare-like effect on neuromuscular function. Bronchospasm can occur with the inhalation of TOBI®. In clinical studies, changes in FEV1 measured after the inhaled dose were similar in the TOBI® and placebo groups. Bronchospasm should be treated as medically appropriate. TOBI® belongs to a class of antibiotics that have been associated with hearing loss, dizziness, kidney damage, and fetal harm. Ringing in the ears and hoarseness were observed in more patients taking TOBI® than in those receiving placebo during research studies. Patients with cystic fibrosis may experience a variety of symptoms, some of which could be related to their medications. If new or worsening symptoms occur, patients should inform their doctor. Hearing: Patients should report any ringing in the ears, dizziness, or changes in hearing to their doctor. Kidney Damage: Patients with a history of kidney problems should inform their doctor. Pregnancy: Patients who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant while on TOBI® should discuss the potential risks with their doctor. Nursing Mothers: Patients who are breastfeeding should consult their doctor before using TOBI®. A Patient Medication Guide with instructions for the proper use of TOBI® is included in the package.
